## Engineer by training. Data analyst by curiosity.

Chemical engineering taught me that every system tells a story, as long as
you measure it carefully. Somewhere between process calculations and renewable
energy research, I realized the part I enjoyed most wasn't the equations. It
was the data, and that moment when a confusing pattern suddenly makes sense.

That curiosity became my career. Today, I help organizations turn scattered
numbers into clear answers. It might be a dashboard a manager checks every
morning, or a model that spots a trend before it becomes a problem. Either
way, my goal is the same: make data easy to understand and easy to act on.

## What I believe

**Clarity beats complexity.** The best insight is the one people actually use.
Teaching STEM has shown me that a clear explanation is worth more than a
clever chart.

**Good decisions start with good data.** I'd rather spend an extra hour
checking the numbers than have anyone act on the wrong ones.

**Data should make a difference.** I'm drawn to work in business intelligence,
engineering, energy and climate, where better data leads to better outcomes
for businesses, communities and the planet.

## Where I'm headed

I'm deepening my skills in AI, machine learning and cybersecurity, because
the future of analytics is smarter, faster and more secure. Wherever data
goes next, I want to help people use it well.

## Beyond the data

When I'm not working with data, I'm spending time with my family. They're my
biggest source of joy and my reminder of why the work matters. Good
decisions, after all, are about people.
